comments.text:
An important perspective is missing here. The source material for AI music platforms like Suno ultimately comes from the work of human musicians. Without that creative input, no product can exist. Framing this as innovation while effectively monetizing other people’s intellectual property feels like selling an illusion—almost as if they’re positioning themselves as modern-day Mozarts. In reality, it often comes across as low-tier marketing built on borrowed creativity.

With Suno reportedly reaching agreements with major rights holders such as Warner Music Group, earlier model outputs (pre-v5) are now subject to stricter licensing considerations. In practical terms, the pool of unlicensed material they could draw from has significantly narrowed.

The backlash surrounding newer versions like v5.5 reflects this shift. A growing number of users—particularly on Reddit—have been vocal about declining output quality compared to earlier models. Many describe the removal of pre-v5 behavior and the perceived degradation in results as a major setback, which, in their view, supports the argument that these systems were heavily dependent on prior data conditions that are no longer available.

comments.text: yeah very true the internet has enabled "more" discovery by giving people access to the world, BUT websites and search engines remain avenues of people finding music but with a million music makers out there the issue of saturation --- commercial SEO domination and likely AI as a new form of search - or even recreation based on their capabilities linked to the information being sought will certainly be transformative. None the less physics says the tree DOES make a noise unless the laws of physics don't apply such as a tree falling in a dream. So yes if a tree is not heard it would still behave with or without the observer. However in a reality where things only occur if the observer encounters them then nothing makes a sound if the observer doesn't hear it. Western Society tends to favour the first view rather than the second, as not everyone can have reality housed around their sensory experience. The logical conclusion is that things occur in predicatable ways providing for a sense of sanity in understanding the world and cause and effect.         As an absolute individual self inflection this of course would never hold true directly only through correlation of cause and effect.          You know its not even saturation itself or SEO or marketting butthe very fact that businesses can choose what they serve to the public and generally will favour things beneficial to serve, for example things they deem legal, or things providing them a direct benefit such as ad placements. That old pay to play model.  This is only made more extreme when commercial interests dominate and there is no more net nuetrility, and legal models are more capably enforced with an increasingly facture and fragmented internet where more and more of the old direct to consumer internet is being handed over to megacorproations that tend to act as gatekeepers of all consumer transactions music included.
